F-01

F-01 Depth

Your price starts from an inch number.

One ruler, read four times. The fill climbs to the depth your report promises.

  1. 3.5 in · about R-10

    What a thin attic reads over a bedroom. The ceiling below is doing a third of its job.

  2. 10 in · about R-30

    Seal first. Top plates, wire holes and light boxes get foam before any fill goes in.

  3. 14 in · about R-42

    Fill to the depth on your report, with baffles keeping the eave vents open.

  4. 17 in · about R-51

    Past R-49, the typical target here. The rulers stay stapled to the rafters for the next inspector.

R per inch is about 3 for blown cellulose (typical). R-49 to R-60 is the typical ENERGY STAR / DOE attic range for climate zone 6.

F-02

F-02 Air leaks first

Fill on top of a leak just hides it.

Warm air rides up through the gaps in your ceiling and melts the snow from underneath. That is your icicle. So we seal before we fill.

Attic air sealing. Top plates, wire holes and light boxes sealed with foam and caulk, each one photographed.

Price the sealing
Seal log one photo per seal, in your report
Seal pointHowProof
01 Top platesFoam, then caulk along the wall topPhotographed
02 Wire holesFoam around every cable runPhotographed
03 Light boxesCaulk at the box edgePhotographed
04 Attic hatchWeatherstrip and an insulated lidPhotographed
05 Then the fillOnly after 01 to 04 are signed offRulers stapled

F-03 Ventilation

The fill stops at the baffle. The roof keeps breathing.

  1. 1

    A baffle at every eave

    Keeps soffit air moving under the roof boards, so the fill never blocks the vents.

  2. 2

    Bath fan venting

    Bath fans that dump into the attic rerouted outside, so moisture stops frosting the roof boards.

  3. 3

    Even depth to the edge

    No low strip over the outside wall, where the brown ceiling stain and the icicles start.

F-07 Homeowner notes

What people read off their own attic.

4.9 from 212 reviews Sample rating

  • Written attic check Sample review

    The report had a depth for each part of the attic. Over our bedroom it was three and a half inches, by the hatch almost nothing. The price matched the report line by line.

    Dale P., Fargo

  • Bonus room over the garage Sample review

    The room over our garage was 58 degrees all January. They found gaps at the floor edge and almost no insulation where it meets the outside wall. Now it holds the same as the rest of the house.

    Nicole V., Horace

  • Old vermiculite: test first Sample review

    They saw the shiny pebbles in our attic and stopped right there. No pressure, just how the lab test works and what our choices were. We had it tested before anything else happened.

    Gary O., Moorhead

  • Rim joist spray foam Sample review

    Wind used to whistle at the top of the basement walls. The foam on the rim joist took one day and the basement family room is finally usable in winter.

    Lisa M., West Fargo

  • Blown-in attic top-up Sample review

    I liked the rulers stapled to the rafters. When our buyer's inspector went up, he read the depth off them and wrote it in his report. Easy.

    Brent A., Dilworth

  • Split-level and ranch walls Sample review

    Our split-level had hollow walls on the windy side. They drilled small holes, filled them and plugged them. Hard to spot from the driveway, and the north bedroom stopped being the cold one.

    Anita R., Casselton
